sanskrit: khaṅgī kirīṭamālī ca kuṇḍalī kavacī tathā | mahorasko mahotsāhaḥ siṃhasaṃhanano yuvā || 6 || brahmaṇā ca kṛtaṃ nāma bilva ityabhiviśrutam | tamindro varayāmāsa rājā tvaṃ bhūtale bhava || 7 || triviṣṭapasya bhūmisthaḥ sakhābhūto mama priyaḥ | dadāmi te vaijayantīṃ mālāmamlānapaṃkajām || 8 ||
english: In the Ādikalpa, O Mahādevī, while Brahmā was meditating out of compassion for all the worlds, the Kalpa trees were born. Among them the Bilva tree is praised as Śrīvṛkṣa. Beneath that tree there was seated a gold-lustred being. He was seen by Brahmā, the creator of the worlds. He was joyously and heartily eating different kinds of soft fruits as well as leaves. His fingers were protected with Godhā-skin gloves. He had a bow and arrows. He was adorned with a crown and earrings. He wore a coat of mail and held a sword. He was a young man with a broad chest and leonine body. He was full of enthusiasm. The famous name Bilva was assigned to him by Brahmā. Indra wooed him: “You do become the king on the earth. Though you are stationed on the earth and I am stationed in Svarga, you can be my dear friend. I shall give you a garland of victory (Vaijayantī) with never-fading lotuses. By its power no weapon shall afflict you in war.”
